findings.title: devnet-mint-token airdrop amount uncapped (baseline #4 regression)
findings.code_snippet:
const tokensFloat = AIRDROP_USD_VALUE / tokenInfo.priceUsd;
const airdropAmount = BigInt(Math.floor(tokensFloat * 10 ** decimals));
findings.description: The $500-USD airdrop converts price to a raw token amount with no upper clamp. priceUsd comes from DexScreener and decimals from token metadata, so a dust-priced token yields a mint of ~5e14 raw tokens per call, drawn from the shared DEVNET_MINT_AUTHORITY_KEYPAIR. The sibling route devnet-airdrop clamps with MIN_RAW/MAX_RAW (route.ts:100); this route has no clamp on either the existing-mint path (:275) or the new-mint path (:388).
findings.flow_analysis: POST /api/devnet-mint-token -> per-IP checkMintRateLimit -> tryFaucetGate (per wallet+token 24h) -> fetchTokenInfo(DexScreener) -> mintTo from shared mint authority. The gate is keyed per (wallet, mainnetCA): fresh wallets or fresh CAs repeat the mint. The per-IP limiter (10/min, Upstash, in-memory fallback) is the only cross-wallet bound.
findings.exploit: Pick a mainnet token with a tiny priceUsd and valid DexScreener metadata; call the endpoint once per wallet/token pair; receive ~5e14 raw tokens per call. Devnet value only, but inflates mirror mints and drains the shared signer.
findings.verdict_rationale: Traced end-to-end in code; the only external dependency is the DexScreener price feed, which is the attacker-chosen input. Baseline #4 is 919 commits old and still present verbatim in both airdrop paths.
findings.attack_value: devnet faucet drain (test tokens, shared signer)

findings.title: Unauthenticated devnet-mirror-mint spends shared wallet SOL (baseline #6, partially fixed)
findings.code_snippet:
const MINT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX = 10;
// ... Upstash slidingWindow limiter, with in-memory fallback when Upstash unconfigured
findings.description: The endpoint remains unauthenticated (by design for the wizard), and every accepted call creates an on-chain SPL mint whose rent and fees are paid by the shared DEVNET_MINT_AUTHORITY wallet. The Upstash 10/min/IP limiter added since the baseline bounds the drain, but the in-memory fallback is per-instance and getClientIp has a misconfig-dependent spoof path (F-06).
findings.flow_analysis: POST /api/devnet-mirror-mint -> getClientIp -> Upstash limiter (or in-memory fallback) -> devnet_mints lookup -> create mint via sealed mint-authority signer. No auth of any kind; the only gates are rate limits.
findings.exploit: Anonymous caller at >10 req/min/IP (or across instances when Upstash is unset, or with spoofed x-real-ip per F-06) creates mints until the shared wallet's SOL is exhausted.
findings.verdict_rationale: Auth absence and the SOL cost are confirmed in code; the drain rate depends on deployment config (Upstash, TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH). Baseline #6 assessed PARTIALLY FIXED.

findings.title: Creator-controlled mark price on creator-run admin-oracle markets listed to all users (oracle rug)
findings.description: The launcher creates and lists admin-oracle markets whose on-chain oracle_authority is the market creator. Delegation to the semi-trusted keeper is a separate, optional step (keeper-cosign + keeper-register). A market registered via POST /api/markets without delegation lists to every user with oracle_mode 'admin', and its creator can then call PushAuthMark (tag 63) directly on-chain with any price up to MAX_ORACLE_PRICE ($1B, lib/oraclePrice.ts:6-8), liquidating or trading against counterparties on that market. The app's own admin push UI was removed (useAdminActions.pushPrice throws), so the attack needs off-app tooling.
findings.flow_analysis: create-market (admin mode only) -> POST /api/markets registers metadata (creator sig, no delegation required) -> /api/markets lists the market to all users -> creator sends PushAuthMark on-chain as oracle_authority with an extreme mark -> users' positions are liquidated / PnL skewed against them. The wizard's normal path delegates to the keeper (checkKeeperReadiness enforces keeper-as-authority only on the keeper-register path, which is optional for listing).
findings.exploit: Create a market, register it, let other users open positions (LP or opposing side), then push an extreme mark on-chain via a direct program call; liquidate them and withdraw profit.
findings.verdict_rationale: All app-side steps traced in code. NOT verified: whether a non-delegated admin-oracle market actually lists and attracts counterparties at HEAD, and the exact on-chain authority check in PushAuthMark (program source is out of repo). This is the one finding that can be high severity against real users.
findings.attack_value: trader funds on a creator-run market (mainnet-relevant class)

findings.title: devnet-pre-fund has no per-IP fund limiter
findings.code_snippet:
NOTE this route has no per-IP fund limiter, unlike /api/playground/faucet,
// /api/auto-fund and /api/devnet-airdrop (see lib/fund-ip-rate-limit.ts).
findings.description: The pre-fund route is documented (in its own shared module) as lacking the per-IP fund limiter every sibling faucet endpoint applies. Only middleware's general 120 req/min/IP and the per-wallet 24h gate apply, and the per-wallet gate is defeated by fresh keypairs. Per call the mint is bounded by MAX_FUNDABLE_REQUIREMENT (10,000 tokens -> 20,000 minted raw) from the shared mint authority.
findings.flow_analysis: POST /api/devnet-pre-fund -> middleware 120/min/IP -> per-wallet 24h claim (Blob-backed) -> mint 2x requirement to caller wallet. Fresh keypairs each get a fresh wallet gate.
findings.exploit: Cycle fresh devnet keypairs and call pre-fund up to 120/min/IP; drain the shared sim-USDC mint authority at up to 20,000 tokens per call.
findings.verdict_rationale: Route code and the module comment both confirm the missing limiter; drain rate bounded by middleware and the per-call cap.

findings.title: Keeper HMAC signatures replayable within 5-minute window (no nonce)
findings.description: The keeper<->app HMAC binds method+path+body+timestamp and is timing-safe, but has no nonce: a captured signature is valid for re-submission of the same body to the same endpoint for 5 minutes. PATCH /api/markets/[slab] additionally accepts the legacy unbound signature form (allowLegacyUnbound=true, route.ts:530) during the rollout transition, which weakens the method/path binding.
findings.flow_analysis: An observer or log-reader who captures x-keeper-timestamp + x-keeper-signature + raw body can re-submit the identical request for 5 minutes. Endpoints affected: POST /api/oracle-keeper/register, PATCH /api/markets/[slab], POST /api/playground/keeper-register (internal hop).
findings.exploit: Capture a keeper HMAC header pair (e.g. from a misconfigured logging path or an http hop - the code enforces https/loopback for KEEPER_INTERNAL_URL, so in practice only log/IPC capture); replay within 5 minutes.
findings.verdict_rationale: Documented unfixed in the code (#2476); capture vector requires an additional defect (HTTPS enforced, loopback enforced). Low severity.

findings.title: Unauthenticated advance-phase route spends CRANK_KEYPAIR SOL (dead instruction in v17)
findings.code_snippet:
const data = encodeAdvanceOraclePhase();
// ... comment: 'AdvanceOraclePhase does not exist in v17 (removed; was v12 tag 92) - this ALWAYS throws'
findings.description: POST /api/oracle/advance-phase has no authentication; any caller supplies a slabAddress and the route builds and sends a CRANK_KEYPAIR-signed transaction (crank pays fees), rate-limited 60/min/IP. On current v17 deployments the instruction always throws before submission, making it dead code with a live unauthenticated entry point.
findings.flow_analysis: POST -> rate limit (60/min/IP) -> loadCrankKeypair -> getLatestBlockhash -> build tx (fee payer = crank) -> send. If v12 tiers were ever re-enabled, anonymous callers could cycle crank-signed txs at 60/min.
findings.exploit: Anonymous POST /api/oracle/advance-phase with arbitrary slab addresses; each successful call spends crank SOL for fees. Currently no-ops because the instruction is removed in v17.
findings.verdict_rationale: Auth absence and server signing confirmed; the SOL spend is currently unreachable (instruction removed), hence low.

findings.title: Per-instance in-memory rate-limit fallbacks bypassable on serverless
findings.description: When UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN are unset (or Upstash init fails), the global 120/min, RPC 600/min, fund-endpoint 10/min and mirror-mint 10/min limits all fall back to per-lambda-instance in-memory windows. Production logs the error but does not fail closed.
findings.flow_analysis: Client sends requests that land on different serverless instances (normal under load); each instance maintains an independent counter, so effective limits multiply by instance count.
findings.exploit: Deploy without Upstash env vars (or wait for a Redis outage), then distribute requests; all per-IP limits collapse to per-instance budgets.
findings.verdict_rationale: Fallback behavior confirmed in code (proxy.ts, upstash-rate-limit.ts, mirror-mint route); exploitation requires a deployment config gap.

findings.title: Slab secret key persisted in plaintext in browser localStorage (baseline #8, intentional)
findings.description: The in-flight-market recovery flow stores the slab keypair's 64-byte secret key in localStorage so the in-UI ReclaimSlabRent path works after tab close. The header comment (2026-05-12) documents the accepted trade-off: bounded amounts, SDK pin + CSP, and the secret is required for rent reclaim of a half-created slab. An XSS with same-origin read can recover the keypair of an unfinished slab.
findings.flow_analysis: saveInFlightMarket() writes {slabAddress, slabSecretKey, ...} to localStorage under 'percolator:in-flight-market:<slab>'. loadLastInFlightMarket()/loadAllInFlightMarkets() read it back for resume/reclaim. No wallet private keys are stored by the app anywhere else.
findings.exploit: XSS on the app reads the slab secret; attacker can sign ReclaimSlabRent for the unfinished slab (rent value only) or complete the market creation flow as the slab key.
findings.verdict_rationale: Confirmed present at HEAD; documented intentional. Value bounded to slab rent / an unfinished market's creation path.

findings.title: getClientIp fails open to spoofable x-real-ip on TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH misconfiguration
findings.description: A non-numeric TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH yields NaN (Math.max(0, NaN) = NaN; NaN > 0 is false), silently skipping the XFF chain and keying every per-IP rate limit on the attacker-controllable x-real-ip header. An explicit TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH=0 does the same. On Vercel, x-real-ip is platform-set, so exposure is misconfiguration or non-Vercel deploys.
findings.flow_analysis: getClientIp() is the key extractor for: proxy.ts global/RPC limits, fund-ip-rate-limit (shared faucet limiter), devnet-mirror-mint, markets/challenge, advance-phase, create-market rate limits.
findings.exploit: Set TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH to a non-numeric value (or 0) on a deployment, then send x-real-ip with a fresh value per request to bypass every per-IP limit.
findings.verdict_rationale: NaN fail-open path confirmed by code reading; exploitation requires a misconfigured or non-Vercel deployment (defaults are safe).

findings.title: Unauthenticated keeper co-sign endpoint exposes privileged partial signatures
findings.code_snippet:
keeper.partialSign(tx);
// ... 'No auth header needed - the keeper co-sign is safe to expose publicly'
findings.description: POST /api/playground/keeper-cosign requires no authentication: any caller can obtain a keeper-keypair partial signature over ConfigureAuthMark + UpdateAssetAuthority(oracle -> keeper) for any (slab, assetIndex<=13), with an attacker-chosen initialMarkE6 <= $1M. Safe by construction for foreign markets (the current oracle authority must co-sign; deployer is fee payer; deployer===keeper aliasing rejected), so the exposure is the privileged-signature-for-the-internet surface itself.
findings.flow_analysis: POST -> validate pubkeys/price (MAX_PRICE_E6 clamp at :153) -> read live marketId/control seqs -> build ConfigureAuthMark + UpdateAssetAuthority -> keeper.partialSign -> return partial tx for the creator to co-sign.
findings.exploit: Anonymous caller requests co-signs for arbitrary (slab, assetIndex) pairs; only their own markets complete. Residual risk: v18 CAS/signer-aliasing edge cases across the 14 asset slots, and zero-cost keeper-keypair signature minting for griefing.
findings.verdict_rationale: Route is unauthenticated by documented design and safe under the traced signer model; the residual risk (v18 multi-asset CAS) needs the deep pass to rule out.
